name: Carcinosarcoma of the cervix uteri
aliases: Malignant mixed Müllerian tumor of the cervix

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Immunohistochemical Diagnostic Criteria for Cervical Carcinosarcoma

criteria.description: Presence of both malignant epithelial (carcinomatous) and malignant mesenchymal (sarcomatous) components on histological examination
Immunohistochemical staining demonstrating epithelial markers (e.g. cytokeratin) in carcinomatous areas and mesenchymal markers (e.g. vimentin) in sarcomatous areas
Exclusion of other primary cervical malignancies such as pure squamous cell carcinoma or sarcoma
Clinical presentation with abnormal vaginal bleeding or cervical mass

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of biphasic malignant epithelial and mesenchymal components with supportive immunohistochemical findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires expert pathological review due to rarity and histological complexity.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Malignant biphasic tumor histology with carcinomatous and sarcomatous elements
searchTerms: tumor with mixed cancer and connective tissue cells
malignant tumor with two cell types
biphasic tumor with carcinoma and sarcoma

common.symptomName: Pelvic mass detected on physical examination

common.notes: May be present due to tumor necrosis or infection

searchTerms: unintentional weight loss and poor appetite
constipation or changes in bowel habits
brain or nerve problems from tumor

rare.notes: Due to tumor necrosis and invasion
searchTerms: open skin wound on tumor site

laboratory: Anemia due to chronic blood loss
Elevated inflammatory markers (e.g. ESR, CRP) in advanced disease
imaging: Pelvic MRI showing heterogeneous cervical mass with possible local invasion
CT scan for staging and detection of metastases
genetic: No specific germline mutations identified; somatic mutations may include TP53 and KRAS alterations
other: Histopathology demonstrating biphasic malignant epithelial and mesenchymal components
Immunohistochemistry positive for cytokeratin and vimentin

distinguishingFeatures: Pure epithelial malignancy without sarcomatous component
Different immunohistochemical profile lacking mesenchymal markers
Pure mesenchymal tumor without carcinomatous elements
Lack of epithelial markers on immunohistochemistry
Benign epithelial component with malignant stromal component

redFlags: Persistent abnormal vaginal bleeding unresponsive to treatment
Evidence of local invasion or distant metastases on imaging
references: Kurman RJ, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Female Reproductive Organs, 4th Edition, 2014.
Pecorelli S. Revised FIGO staging for carcinoma of the cervix. Int J Gynaecol Obstet. 2009.
Orphanet: Carcinosarcoma of the cervix uteri (ORPHA:213787).
